reported_regression: The safe new-chat handoff button was not directly visible.
The Diagnostics cards lost their established visual treatment and became a long unstructured list.
Active Path Discovery was not available as a first-class Diagnostics item.
The Diagnostics screen was appended below the existing full-height app wrapper, requiring a large scroll before its content appeared.
The canonical Active Path card could miss the final Control screen because its fixed mount timers expired before the nested app frame finished loading.

repair.diagnostics_layout: Restores the established bold card, icon, subtitle, and chevron treatment with bounded responsive spacing.
repair.diagnostics_viewport: Anchors the Diagnostics owner surface to the visible app viewport below Launcher and Resident and above the bottom navigation, and opens each view at its first action.
repair.safe_handoff: Places Copy New Chat Safe Handoff directly above the Diagnostics card list and preserves the App Orchestrator Status copy.
repair.active_path: Adds Active Path Discovery directly above the fold and as a first-class Diagnostics card with canonical and bounded reports kept separate.
repair.active_path_mount: Replaces the canonical owner's fixed mount-timer race with target-bounded frame-load and DOM mount-target events; no recurring polling or helper takeover is introduced.
repair.owner_delegation: Manual rerun requests the canonical PMPActivePathDiscoveryMachineV1 owner API; Diagnostics never writes either Active Path report.
repair.handoff_context: Adds this restoration evidence to the one-button new-chat packet.

checks: Diagnostics occupies the visible viewport at y=0 with scrollTop=0.
Copy New Chat Safe Handoff is the first visible action.
Active Path Discovery is the second visible action and a first-class card.
The restored bold icon, subtitle, chevron card layout is visible.
The canonical Active Path Discovery Control card survives the final nested-frame load.
Active Path detail exposes rerun and copy actions.

claim_ceiling: Diagnostics presentation and read-only evidence restoration only.
